findings.observed: Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises.
findings.expected: Provide a localized banner image (e.g. banner-fr.png) with the text translated to French: "Un financement adapté à vos projets / Taux compétitifs. Conditions claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The homepage banner image is served from /static/img/banner-en.png on the French page too, showing untranslated English text ("Financing that fits your plans", "Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises.") baked into the image.
The site footer copyright notice is left in English on the French page.

The hero subtitle uses the informal "tu" register (Découvre, tes) while the rest of the site (e.g. "Ouvrir une session", "Appliquer pour un prêt") uses the formal "vous" register, creating an inconsistent register.

On the French apply form, the validation error for the "Nom complet" field is left in English ("This field is required.") while all other fields on the same form correctly show "Ce champ est obligatoire."

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande pour 5 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: On the loan application confirmation page, the French confirmation message shows the raw unreplaced template placeholder "{montant}" instead of the formatted loan amount, while the English version correctly interpolates "$5,000.00".

The checkbox label is translated with the opposite meaning: English "Pay later" (deferred first payment) becomes French "Payer maintenant" ("Pay now"), even though the help text below still correctly says the first payment is deferred by 30 days.

The estimated monthly payment amount on the French calculator page is shown in US currency format ($450.91) instead of Canadian French format (450,91 $), unlike the application confirmation page which correctly formats amounts as "5 000,00 $".

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Accusation" is a mistranslation of "charges" here; in French "accusation" means a legal accusation, not a fee. The correct term is "frais".

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve d'approbation de crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the qualifier "subject to credit approval" that is present in the English version, changing the disclosed conditions of the offer.
The modal's close link is mistranslated as "Proche" (the adjective meaning "near"), instead of the verb "Fermer" meaning to close a dialog.
The "Recent transactions" section heading on the dashboard is left untranslated in French, even though the summary text just above it correctly says "3 opérations récentes".

Transaction dates in the French dashboard table are formatted as US-style MM/DD/YYYY ("09/15/2026"), while the English version correctly uses ISO format ("2026-09-15"). This is both wrong for fr-CA convention and ambiguous/misleading (could be misread as day/month).

findings.expected: Link should point to /fr/calculator when on the French dashboard.
findings.description: On the French dashboard, the "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link incorrectly points to the English calculator page (/en/calculator) instead of /fr/calculator, dropping the user out of French unexpectedly.
"Balance" is an anglicism in this banking context; standard fr-CA banking terminology uses "solde" (e.g. "Solde du compte").

"Déclaration mensuelle" is the wrong banking term for "statement" (which means an account statement); "déclaration" means "declaration" (e.g. tax declaration). The correct fr-CA banking term is "relevé mensuel".
